items.title: Harry Fairconnetue Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: we had Mr. Hooper, the mayor of Derrida's son-in-law, who booked us around that territory.

ctx.x: Let's see. Uh, so, Clarence's band would play on a tour, you say, and played around Omaha. You played fairs?
We played practically everything with that band. Uh-huh. And, when he was the booking agent, he'd go ahead of us. Uh-huh. And I was managing the band. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh.

I'd pick up the receipts, pay off the man, and send his parada back to him. He bought a bus, and I'd send his bus fare back to him and his man's money for, you know, like a record guy. He booked for a while, and then we'd get to places and a place where pretty good dancing was going on. We had around Arkansas, we had Mr. Hooper, the mayor of Derrida's son-in-law, who booked us around that territory.
